members.title: Kraków shooting suspect who killed six has died, say police in Poland
members.lead: Terrorism investigation continues after 24-year-old opened fire in market square, leaving 16 injured A gunman who killed six people, including a British man, and injured 16 in a rare mass shooting in a busy market square in Kraków has died in hospital, Polish police said. The suspect, a 24-year-old Polish national who has not yet been officially named, opened fire in the city’s main square on Saturday afternoon in an attack that a government minister said was probably influenced by far-right ideologies. He was wounded during a shootout with police and taken to hospital in a critical condition. Continue reading...

members.lead: The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has said some progress had been made on what the “security infrastructure” of Ukraine and Europe could look like after the war with Russia. Rubio’s comments on Sunday come as Russia-Ukraine negotiations under US mediation have been set for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, with the talks expected to focus on postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and steps to end the war. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Trump’s son-in-law, will represent the US during the talks. The Kremlin insisted this morning that no European officials will be there, rebuffing France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noel Barrot, who said French representatives would ‌be present.
